It reflects the actual scale of capital locked in by the enterprise at the beginning of the period to maintain and conduct business activities.

Beginning long-term liabilities refer to the book value of debts with a repayment period exceeding one year that an enterprise bears at the start of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter). It reflects the enterprise's long-term financial leverage level at the beginning of the period.

Beginning long-term assets refer to the total carrying value of assets owned by an enterprise at the start of an accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter), which are expected to have a useful life exceeding one accounting period (typically more than one year or one operating cycle). These assets generally include fixed assets, intangible assets, long-term equity investments, etc., and form the foundation for the enterprise's long-term operations and value creation.

Beginning long-term capital refers to the total amount of capital with long-term characteristics that an enterprise possesses at the start of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or a quarter). It is typically used to measure the capital base available for long-term investment and operations at the beginning of the period and serves as a crucial starting point for calculating financial metrics such as return on capital.

Beginning non-current assets refer to the book value of assets held by an enterprise at the start of an accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter) that are not expected to be realized or consumed within one year or within one operating cycle exceeding one year.

Period t refers to the specific time interval or number of periods from the present point in time at which a future cash flow occurs in financial and financial calculations. It is commonly used in discounting calculations to determine the present value of future cash flows.

Expected value is a method that associates an amount with each possible outcome of a probability distribution, which can be simply understood as the weighted average considering various possible outcomes and their probabilities of occurrence. In financial management, it is often used as a reference benchmark for evaluating investment returns or costs.

The Expected Cash Flow Method is an approach used to estimate the future cash flows of an asset or investment project. It calculates the weighted average (expected value) of future cash flows by considering various possible future operating scenarios (e.g., good, average, poor performance) and their respective probabilities of occurrence, thereby more reasonably reflecting the uncertainty of future cash flows.

Ending net assets refer to the residual value of a company's total assets minus total liabilities at the end of a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or fiscal year), representing the total equity owned by the company's owners at that point in time.

term_en.name: Total Net Assets at Period End

english: Total Net Assets at Period End

definition_en: Total net assets at period end refers to the total equity attributable to owners (shareholders) that remains after subtracting total liabilities from total assets at the conclusion of a specific accounting period (such as month-end, quarter-end, or year-end). It represents the true value of wealth belonging to the owners at that point in time.

term_en.name: Weighted Average Number of Common Shares Outstanding at Period End

chinese: 发行在外普通股加权平均数
当期普通股加权平均数
english: Weighted Average Number of Common Shares Outstanding

definition_en: The weighted average number of common shares outstanding at period end refers to the number of shares calculated by weighting the shares issued at different points in time according to their proportion of the reporting period in circulation. This calculation is performed to more accurately reflect the actual number of common shares available throughout the period when computing metrics such as earnings per share for a financial reporting period (e.g., quarter or year), considering that the number of common shares may change due to new share issuances or share repurchases during the period.

term_en.name: Ending Work-in-Process and Semi-finished Goods Value

english: Value of Work-in-Process at Period End

definition_en: Ending work-in-process and semi-finished goods value refers to the estimated or accounted value of all unfinished products and semi-finished goods still in the production process at the end of a specific accounting period (such as month, quarter, or year). It reflects the inventory value remaining on the production line that has not yet reached a saleable state at the period-end date.

term_en.name: Ending Work in Process Inventory Cost

definition_en: Ending work in process inventory cost refers to the total accumulated costs of products that are not yet completed and remain in the processing or assembly stage on the production line at the end of an accounting period (such as a month, quarter, or year). These costs typically include direct materials, direct labor, and allocated manufacturing overhead already incurred. This cost serves as the basis for calculating the cost of goods completed during the period and is reported as part of inventory on the balance sheet.

term_en.name: Ending Work in Process and Semi-finished Goods Cost

english: Ending Work-in-Process and Semi-finished Goods Cost
Closing WIP and Semi-finished Goods Cost

definition_en: Ending work in process and semi-finished goods cost refers to the total accumulated production costs of all products that are not yet completed and remain in the production process (work in process), as well as intermediate products that have completed certain production steps but are not yet final finished goods (semi-finished goods), at the end of a specific accounting period (such as month-end, quarter-end, or year-end).

The ending balance of notes receivable refers to the total book value of notes receivable that have not yet matured or been settled at the end of a specific accounting period (such as month-end, quarter-end, or year-end). It reflects the amount of receivables held by the enterprise at that point in time, consisting of commercial drafts (including trade acceptance bills and bank acceptance bills).

term_en.name: Total Shares Outstanding at Period End

english: Total Shares Outstanding at Period End

definition_en: Total shares outstanding at period end refers to the aggregate number of all issued and outstanding shares held by shareholders at the conclusion of a specific accounting period (such as quarter-end or year-end). It serves as a critical base figure for calculating metrics such as dividend per share and net asset value per share.

chinese: 资产负债表日所有者权益

definition_en: Ending owner's equity refers to the book value of the residual interest attributable to the owners (shareholders) of an enterprise after deducting total liabilities from total assets at the end of a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a fiscal year). It reflects the net asset position of the enterprise at the end of the period.

term_en.name: Total Interest-Free Liabilities at Period End

english: Total Interest-Free Liabilities at Period End

definition_en: Total interest-free liabilities at period end refers to the aggregate amount of all liability items that do not require interest payments at the conclusion of a specific accounting period (such as quarter-end or year-end). These liabilities typically include operating liabilities such as accounts payable, advance receipts, contract liabilities, employee compensation payable, and taxes payable.

term_en.name: Total Common Shares Outstanding at Period End

chinese: 报告期末普通股总股数
english: Number of Common Shares Outstanding at Period End

definition_en: Total common shares outstanding at period end refers to the total number of shares issued and held by common shareholders at the conclusion of a specific accounting period (such as quarter-end or year-end). It serves as a crucial base figure for calculating key financial metrics such as earnings per share and dividends per share.

Terminal value per share refers to the expected value of each share of stock at a future point in time, calculated based on a compound growth model at the end of a specific investment horizon. It reflects the amount to which the current value per share can grow by the end of the period, given a specified rate of return and holding period.

Ending retained earnings balance refers to the final book value of the retained earnings account at the end of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or a quarter). Retained earnings represent the accumulated after-tax profits generated by the company over the years that are retained within the business for reinvestment or future distribution, primarily consisting of two components: surplus reserves and undistributed profits.

The ending balance of surplus reserve refers to the remaining amount in a company's surplus reserve account at the end of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter). It represents the total amount of reserve funds accumulated and retained from after-tax profits up to that point in time, designated for specific purposes such as covering losses or increasing capital.

Ending book balance refers to the calculated remaining amount of an accounting item or account at the end of a specific accounting period (such as month-end, quarter-end, or year-end), based on accounting records. It reflects the final result of the account after considering the beginning balance and all additions and reductions during the current period.

Terminal asset disposal proceeds refer to the cash or cash equivalent income obtained by an enterprise at the end of an accounting period (such as a quarter or a fiscal year) through the sale, transfer, retirement, or other disposal of its long-term assets (such as fixed assets, intangible assets).

The End-of-Period Debt-to-Asset Ratio refers to the ratio of total liabilities to total assets at the conclusion of a specific accounting period (e.g., month-end, quarter-end, year-end). It measures the proportion of a company's total assets financed through debt, reflecting the firm's long-term solvency and financial leverage level.

english: Carrying Amount of Assets at Period End

definition_en: Ending book value of assets refers to the net value of various assets listed on a company's balance sheet after accounting treatments at the end of a specific accounting period (such as month-end, quarter-end, or year-end). It typically equals the original value (acquisition cost) of the asset minus accumulated depreciation (or amortization) and any provision for asset impairment, reflecting the carrying value of the asset on the reporting date.

Ending Capital Employed refers to the total amount of capital actually invested and utilized by a company to sustain its business operations at the end of a specific accounting period (e.g., a quarter or fiscal year). It is commonly used to measure the comprehensive usage of both debt capital and equity capital at the period-end point, serving as a key foundational data point for calculating performance metrics such as Economic Value Added (EVA).

english: Long Term Liabilities at Period End

definition_en: Ending long-term liabilities refer to the total amount of debt with a repayment period exceeding one year or one operating cycle, as presented on a company's balance sheet at the end of an accounting period (such as month-end, quarter-end, or year-end). It reflects the debt burden that the company needs to repay over a relatively long period in the future.

Ending long-term assets refer to the total assets owned by an enterprise at the end of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter) that are expected to be held for more than one year or one operating cycle. These assets are typically not intended for sale or liquidation in the short term and are primarily used for the enterprise's long-term operations and investment activities.

Ending long-term capital refers to the total amount of funding sources available for long-term use that a company possesses at the end of an accounting period (e.g., year-end, quarter-end). It typically consists of shareholders' equity, long-term liabilities, and working capital (or net working capital), reflecting the stable capital base that supports the company's long-term assets and operations.

Futures price refers to the agreed-upon price between buyers and sellers in the futures market for the delivery of a specified quantity and quality of an underlying asset at a specific future date. It is typically formed based on the spot price plus carrying costs (such as storage fees, insurance, financing interest, etc.).

term_en.name: Number of Common Shares Repurchased During the Period

english: Number of Common Shares Repurchased During the Period

definition_en: Number of Common Shares Repurchased During the Period refers to the total quantity of a listed company's issued common shares bought back from the open market using its own funds within a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a fiscal year).

Period Tax Payable refers to the amount of income tax that a taxpayer is required to pay to the tax authority for a specific tax period (such as a month, quarter, or year), calculated in accordance with tax laws and regulations. It is typically derived from the taxable income for that period and the applicable tax rate.

term_en.name: Total Trading Volume for the Period

definition_en: Total trading volume for the period refers to the cumulative total number of shares of a specific stock traded in all market transactions during a specified time frame (such as a day, week, or month), typically measured in shares. It is a key indicator for measuring market activity and liquidity.

term_en.name: Number of Newly Issued Common Shares During the Period

english: Number of Newly Issued Common Shares During the Period

definition_en: The number of newly issued common shares during the period refers to the total quantity of common stock newly issued and sold to investors by a company within a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a year), for reasons such as raising capital, conducting business combinations (e.g., non-common control mergers), or debt-to-equity conversions. It is one of the important underlying data points for determining changes in the weighted average number of common shares outstanding when calculating financial metrics such as earnings per share.

Period cash flow refers to the total net inflow or outflow of cash and cash equivalents generated by a company through operating activities, investing activities, and financing activities during a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a year). It reflects the company's ability to generate and utilize cash during that period and is a key indicator for assessing liquidity, financial health, and operating performance.

Periodic dividend or interest refers to the cash return received by investors for holding securities (such as stocks or bonds) during a specific period (e.g., a quarter, half-year, or year). For stocks, this typically refers to dividends distributed by a company to shareholders from retained earnings; for bonds or deposits, it refers to interest income calculated based on principal and the agreed interest rate. It is an essential component in calculating the periodic rate of return on securities.

Period expenses refer to costs incurred by an enterprise for organizing and managing production and operating activities. These expenses are not directly associated with the production of specific products, cannot be directly allocated to product costs, occur over time irrespective of changes in production volume, and are entirely borne by the current period's profit and loss. They primarily include administrative expenses, selling expenses, and financial expenses.

english: Selling, General and Administrative Expense Ratio

definition_en: The Period Expense Ratio is a key financial metric for measuring a company's operational efficiency. It refers to the percentage of total period expenses incurred during a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a year) relative to the operating revenue for the same period. Period expenses typically include administrative expenses, selling expenses, and financial expenses. These costs are not directly associated with the production of specific products or services but are necessary for maintaining overall business operations. A lower ratio generally indicates stronger expense control capabilities and higher operational efficiency.

Term risk premium refers to the additional rate of return required by investors for holding long-term bonds or assets, due to the risk of price fluctuations caused by future interest rate changes. It constitutes a component of the nominal interest rate or required rate of return, compensating for the increased uncertainty associated with longer investment horizons.

term_en.name: Unrealized Intercompany Transaction Gains and Losses

english: Unrealized Gains or Losses from Internal Transactions

definition_en: Unrealized intercompany transaction gains and losses refer to the portion of internal profit or loss embedded in the transaction price when goods, services, or assets are traded within a corporate group (e.g., between a parent company and its subsidiaries), before the subject matter of the transaction (such as inventory or fixed assets) is fully sold to or consumed by external third parties outside the group. These gains and losses must be eliminated in the preparation of consolidated financial statements to prevent overstatement of the group's overall profit or asset value.

term_en.name: Present Value of Unguaranteed Residual Value

english: Present Value of Unguaranteed Residual Value

definition_en: The present value of unguaranteed residual value refers to the current value, discounted to the beginning of the lease term at a specified discount rate (typically the implicit interest rate in the lease), of the unguaranteed residual value of a leased asset at the end of the lease term (i.e., the portion of the estimated residual value not guaranteed by the lessee or a third party). It is a significant factor for lessors when calculating the net investment in the lease and determining the implicit interest rate in the lease.

Unamortized bond issuance costs refer to the expenses incurred by an enterprise when issuing bonds that have not yet been allocated to the profit or loss of each period over the bond's term. These costs are initially recognized as part of the bond's carrying amount, as an adjustment to an asset or liability, and are subsequently amortized using the effective interest method to reflect the true cost of financing of the bond.

Unamortized bond discount refers to the remaining portion of the difference between a bond's face value and its lower issuance price that has not yet been allocated to interest expense through amortization (i.e., periodic recognition) over the bond's life. It is a contra account to the carrying value of bonds payable.

Unamortized bond premium refers to the portion of the premium arising from issuing bonds at a price above their face value that has not yet been amortized into interest expense over the bond's life. This remaining premium must be amortized in each accounting period until maturity to adjust the actual interest expense.

Future single cash flow refers to a specific amount of cash that a company expects to receive or pay at a particular future point in time. It is an estimate of a single future cash inflow or outflow based on current information and reasonable assumptions, serving as a fundamental element for asset valuation, investment decision-making, and financial analysis.

Future single cash flow refers to a single expected cash inflow or outflow generated or required by an asset, project, or business operation at a specific future point in time. It serves as fundamental data for asset valuation, investment decision-making, and financial forecasting.

term_en.name: Present Value of Future Periodic Payments

definition_en: The present value of future periodic payments refers to the sum of the values, discounted to the current point in time at a specific discount rate (typically the loan interest rate or market rate), of all amounts required to be repaid in future payment periods (e.g., monthly, quarterly) for a loan or debt. It represents the theoretical total amount of funds needed at the current point in time to settle all future debt obligations, commonly used to calculate the outstanding principal balance of a loan or to evaluate prepayment options.

The present value of future payments refers to the total current value of all remaining payments (including principal and interest) for a loan or debt over its remaining term, discounted at a specific discount rate (typically the loan's interest rate). Under equal principal and interest payments or equal principal payment methods, this value typically equals the current outstanding principal balance.

Expected future period returns refer to the forecast or estimation of the potential income amount that an asset or investment may generate in each specific future period (e.g., annually, quarterly). It is an assessment of future cash flows or returns based on current information, market trends, and assumptions, commonly used in asset valuation and investment decision-making.

Projected Pension Benefit Payments refer to the total sum or sequence of pension amounts expected to be paid to pension recipients in future periods (e.g., monthly, annually) based on a pension plan or insurance contract under specific actuarial assumptions (such as discount rate, mortality rate, salary growth rate, etc.). It serves as the basis for assessing the present value of pension liabilities.

Future selling price refers to the projected sales price of a product or service at a specific future period, based on factors such as market research, cost analysis, and competitive conditions. It is a key input variable in financial forecasting, investment decision-making, and valuation models (such as discounted cash flow models).

term_en.name: Present Value of Future Salary Increases

english: Present Value of Future Salary Increases

definition_en: The present value of future salary increases refers to the current value, discounted at a specified rate, of the incremental benefit obligations arising from employees' expected future salary growth (e.g., due to inflation, promotion, performance, etc.) in the accounting measurement of long-term employee benefits such as pension liabilities. It reflects the impact of future compensation changes on the current assessment of liabilities.

term_en.name: Present Value of Future Cash Inflows

chinese: 预计未来现金流量现值
资产未来现金流量现值
english: Present Value of Future Cash Inflows
Present Value of Future Cash Flows

definition_en: Present Value of Future Cash Inflows refers to the total current value of the expected cash inflows from an asset or investment in different future periods, discounted to the present point using an appropriate discount rate. It reflects the current worth of future cash inflows after considering the time value of money.

term_en.name: Present Value of Future Cash Flows

chinese: 预计未来现金流量现值
资产未来现金流量现值
english: Present Value of Future Cash Flows

definition_en: Present Value of Future Cash Flows refers to the total current value of the cash flows that an asset or business is expected to generate in future periods, discounted back to the present point in time using an appropriate discount rate. It serves as a critical foundation for assessing the fair value of assets, making investment decisions, and conducting impairment tests.

Future lease payments refer to the total rental payments that a lessee is obligated to pay to the lessor over the remaining lease term as stipulated in the lease contract. In accounting treatment, it is typically used to calculate the present value of operating lease liabilities or finance lease liabilities.

Expected future returns refer to the forecast and estimation of potential income or returns that an asset, investment, or project may generate over a specific future period, based on existing information and assumptions under conditions of uncertainty.

term_en.name: Total Weekly Trading Volume of Both Exchanges

chinese: 本周沪深两市总成交额
english: Total Weekly Turnover of Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges

definition_en: Total weekly trading volume of both exchanges refers to the sum of the trading value of all listed stocks on the Shanghai Stock Exchange and the Shenzhen Stock Exchange during the week (typically the five trading days from Monday to Friday). It reflects the trading activity and capital flow scale of the entire A-share market for the week.

Current Year Borrowings refer to the total amount of new loans obtained by an enterprise within the current fiscal year through borrowing funds from banks, other financial institutions, or creditors. It reflects the scale of external financing for the enterprise in a specific year and serves as important baseline data for calculating financial costs such as construction period interest.

term_en.name: Taxable Income for the Current Year

english: Taxable Income for the Current Year

definition_en: Taxable income for the current year refers to the income amount calculated according to tax laws on which an enterprise is liable to pay corporate income tax within a tax year. It is derived from the enterprise's total revenue, minus non-taxable income, tax-exempt income, various statutory deductions, and allowable losses carried forward from previous years.

term_en.name: Increase in Owners' Equity for the Current Year

chinese: 所有者权益本年增加额
english: Increase in Owners' Equity for the Year

definition_en: The increase in owners' equity for the current year refers to the difference between the total owners' equity at the end of the current year and the total owners' equity at the end of the previous year, reflecting the net increase in equity achieved by the enterprise through operational accumulation, capital contributions, and other means within an accounting year.

Current Year Amount refers to the cumulative occurrence of relevant financial indicators (such as revenue, cost, profit) from January 1st of the current accounting year to the current reporting period (e.g., end of a month or quarter) in a company's financial statements (e.g., income statement). It reflects the cumulative progress of the indicator within the current year.

term_en.name: Current Year Dividend Per Share Increase

definition_en: Current Year Dividend Per Share Increase refers to the absolute amount by which the dividend per share declared or distributed by a company in the current year exceeds the dividend per share amount from the previous year. It is a key component in calculating the dividend growth rate.

Current Year Sales Revenue refers to the total income obtained by an enterprise within the current accounting year through its principal operating activities, such as selling goods, providing services, or transferring the right to use assets. It reflects the scale and results of the enterprise's core business during that year.

Current year sales volume refers to the total quantity of products or services sold by an enterprise through the sale of goods or provision of services within the current fiscal year. It is a core quantitative indicator for measuring the scale of the enterprise's market sales activities during the year.

Current Year Sales Revenue refers to the total income obtained by an enterprise within the current fiscal year through daily business activities such as selling goods, providing services, or transferring the right to use assets. It reflects the enterprise's primary operating results and market scale over a one-year period.

english: Current Year Sales Revenue Growth Amount
Sales Growth Amount for the Year

definition_en: Current Year Sales (Operating) Revenue Increase refers to the absolute amount by which a company's main business revenue (or sales revenue) has grown in the current fiscal year compared to the previous fiscal year. It serves as the foundational data for calculating financial metrics such as sales growth rate and reflects the absolute growth in the company's sales scale.

term_en.name: Actual Unit Cost of Each Batch Purchased in the Current Month

chinese: 本月批次进货单位成本
当月各批采购实际单价
english: Actual Unit Cost of This Month's Batches Purchased

definition_en: Refers to the average unit cost calculated by dividing the total actual cost incurred for inventory (such as raw materials, goods, etc.) purchased in batches during the current month by the quantity of that batch. The actual cost typically includes purchase price, related taxes, transportation fees, loading and unloading charges, insurance premiums, and other costs attributable to the acquisition of inventory.

term_en.name: Quantity of Purchases by Batch in Current Month

english: Quantity of Purchases by Batch in Current Month

definition_en: Quantity of purchases by batch in the current month refers to the physical quantity of inventory (such as raw materials, merchandise, etc.) purchased or acquired by an enterprise in different batches within the current month. It reflects the scale of purchases, categorized by different purchase orders or receipt batches, during a specific period. This data serves as a fundamental basis for calculating inventory costs, conducting inventory management, and performing cost analysis.

Current Month Amount refers to the cumulative value of relevant economic transactions or financial indicators occurring within the current reporting month (typically from the beginning to the end of the month) in financial accounting and reporting. It is used to reflect the operating results or financial position of an enterprise within a specific month and constitutes an important component of the current period indicators.

term_en.name: Current Period Production and Sales Volume

english: Current Period Production and Sales Volume
Production and Sales of the Period

definition_en: Current period production and sales volume refers to the quantity of products actually completed in production and sold by an enterprise within the current accounting period (such as monthly, quarterly, or annual). It reflects the operational output and market absorption capacity of the enterprise during a specific timeframe and serves as crucial foundational data for cost analysis, profit forecasting, and budget preparation.

term_en.name: Total Interest-bearing Debt for the Period

english: Total Interest-Bearing Debt for the Current Period

definition_en: Total interest-bearing debt for the period refers to the aggregate amount of all debt obligations on which interest must be paid during the current accounting period (such as the current quarter or fiscal year). These obligations typically include bank borrowings, issued bonds, and financing lease liabilities under long-term payables.

Current Period Utilization Amount typically refers to the actual amount of resources, funds, or budget consumed or expended within a specific accounting period (such as a month, quarter, or year). In financial statements of revenues and expenditures, it often corresponds to 'Current Period Revenue' and is used to calculate 'Current Period Balance'.

Current Period Value refers to the amount of financial data calculated or recorded for a specific reporting period (e.g., monthly, quarterly, annual) in financial statements (such as the income statement or cash flow statement). It reflects the actual occurrence or cumulative amount of the relevant items during that period.

term_en.name: Net Operating Assets for the Current Period

definition_en: Net operating assets for the current period refer to the net value of assets used for core business operations (excluding financial investment activities) within the current accounting period. It equals operating assets minus operating liabilities, reflecting the scale of the company's own capital actually invested in operating activities.

term_en.name: Current Period Debt Principal and Interest Due

english: Current Matured Debt Principal and Interest
Debt Service Due in Current Period

definition_en: Current Period Debt Principal and Interest Due refers to the total sum of debt principal that must be repaid and the associated interest that must be paid by an enterprise within the current accounting period (e.g., the current year or quarter), as stipulated in the loan agreements. It is a crucial indicator for measuring an enterprise's short-term debt repayment pressure.

Current labor force, also known as the contemporaneous labor force, refers to the total population within a country or region during the current statistical period (such as a quarter or a year) that is of working age, possesses the capacity to work, and is either employed or actively seeking employment. It serves as the foundational data for calculating indicators such as labor force growth rate.

Current unit price refers to the average price corresponding to each unit of product sold or produced by an enterprise during the current accounting period. It serves as a fundamental indicator for measuring product pricing levels, calculating sales revenue, and analyzing price fluctuations.

term_en.name: Production Costs Incurred in Current Period

english: Production Costs Incurred in Current Period

definition_en: Production costs incurred in the current period refer to the various production expenditures, expressed in monetary terms, that are actually incurred by an enterprise during the current accounting period for producing goods or providing services. They primarily include expenses such as direct materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead.

Current period sales revenue refers to the total revenue earned by an enterprise during the current accounting period (such as monthly, quarterly, or annual) through its principal operating activities, including the sale of goods or provision of services.

Current Period Increase Amount refers to the total sum of increases in the amount of a specific accounting account (such as assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses, etc.) resulting from economic transactions during the current accounting period. It is one of the key elements in calculating the ending balance of an account.

term_en.name: Original Value of Operating Long-term Assets Disposed in Current Period

chinese: 本期处置固定资产原值
本期清理长期资产原值
处置经营长期资产账面原值
english: Original Value of Disposed Operating Long-term Assets in Current Period
Book Value of Long-lived Assets Disposed

definition_en: Original Value of Operating Long-term Assets Disposed in Current Period refers to the historical cost value at initial recognition of fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets used in the enterprise's daily business operations that were disposed of during the current accounting period (such as the current quarter or fiscal year) through means such as sale, scrapping, damage, external investment, non-monetary asset exchange, or debt restructuring. It reflects the scale of historical cost of long-term assets withdrawn from operating activities during the current period.

term_en.name: Decrease in Paid-in Capital for the Current Period

english: Current Period Reduction in Paid-in Capital
Decrease in Contributed Capital for the Period

definition_en: Decrease in Paid-in Capital for the Current Period refers to the amount by which the capital actually received from shareholders (i.e., paid-in capital or share capital) is reduced during the current accounting period, due to reasons such as shareholder withdrawals, share repurchases by the company, or capital reductions.

term_en.name: Increase in Paid-in Capital for the Current Period

english: Increase in Paid-in Capital for the Current Period
Current Period Addition to Paid-in Capital

definition_en: The increase in paid-in capital for the current period refers to the amount by which the portion of the registered capital actually received from shareholders' contributions increases during the current accounting period, through means such as investor contributions, transfers from capital reserves or surplus reserves.

Current Period Employment refers to the total number of individuals in a country or region who are actually engaged in paid work or self-employment during a specific statistical reporting period (such as a quarter or a year). It serves as fundamental data for measuring labor market conditions and calculating related economic indicators (such as the employment rate and labor force growth rate).

term_en.name: Cost of Goods Sold Allocation of Markup

english: Cost of Goods Sold Markup Allocation

definition_en: In commercial retail enterprises using the retail inventory method, this refers to the portion of the difference between the selling price and the purchase price of goods that needs to be calculated and allocated to the cost of goods sold at the end of an accounting period (e.g., month-end). Its purpose is to adjust the selling price of inventory to its actual cost and accurately calculate the current period's cost of sales and gross profit.

term_en.name: Net Increase in Accounts Payable for the Period

chinese: 本期应付账款增加净额
english: Net Increase in Accounts Payable for the Period

definition_en: Net increase in accounts payable for the period refers to the net change in the total accounts payable of an enterprise during a specific accounting period. It is calculated by subtracting the accounts payable repaid or reduced during the period from the newly incurred accounts payable, reflecting the net amount of new, unpaid liabilities arising from the purchase of goods or acceptance of services during that period.

term_en.name: Decrease in Accounts Receivable for the Period

english: Decrease in Accounts Receivable for the Period

definition_en: Decrease in Accounts Receivable for the Period refers to the net reduction in the balance of a company's accounts receivable account during a specific accounting period (such as a month, quarter, or year). This typically indicates that the company collected more cash from customers than the amount of new credit sales generated during the period, reflecting an improvement in collection efficiency or an adjustment in sales policies.

term_en.name: Increase in Accounts Receivable for the Period

english: Increase in Accounts Receivable for the Current Period

definition_en: The increase in accounts receivable for the period refers to the amount of newly generated, uncollected accounts receivable arising from credit sales and other means during the current accounting period. It represents the portion of current period sales not immediately converted into cash receipts and is a key component in calculating the ending balance of accounts receivable.

term_en.name: Cash Payments for Costs and Expenses in Current Period

chinese: 当期成本费用现金支出
本期现金支付成本费用
english: Cash Payment for Costs and Expenses in Current Period
Current Period Cash Outlay for Costs

definition_en: Cash payments for costs and expenses in the current period refer to the total amount of cash actually disbursed by an enterprise during the current accounting period (such as a quarter or a year) to cover various costs and expenses, including main business costs, operating expenses, and administrative expenses. It serves as the fundamental data for calculating financial indicators such as the cash payment ratio for costs and expenses.

term_en.name: Total Owner's Equity for the Current Period

definition_en: Total owner's equity for the current period refers to the aggregate value of all net assets attributable to the owners (shareholders) of an enterprise at the end of the current accounting period (such as the current year or quarter). It represents the residual interest belonging to the owners after deducting all liabilities from the enterprise's assets.

term_en.name: Current Period Technology Level Indicator Value

english: Current Period Technical Level Indicator Value
Technical Level Index Value for the Period

definition_en: The Current Period Technology Level Indicator Value is a quantitative measure used to assess an enterprise's level of technological development or the outcomes of its technology investments during the current reporting period (e.g., current year, current quarter). It typically serves as the base data for calculating dynamic indicators such as the technology level growth rate, reflecting the enterprise's technological status within a specific timeframe.

term_en.name: Raw Materials Put into Production in Current Period

english: Raw Materials Consumed in Current Period

definition_en: Raw materials put into production in the current period refer to the cost of raw materials actually requisitioned and put into the production process for manufacturing products or providing services during the current accounting period (such as a month or a quarter). It is typically calculated by taking the beginning raw materials inventory, adding raw materials purchased during the period, and subtracting the ending raw materials inventory.

Current period depreciation refers to the depreciation amount calculated according to established depreciation methods (such as straight-line method, units-of-production method, double-declining balance method, etc.) based on the wear and tear of fixed assets during the current accounting period (e.g., an accounting year or month), and recorded as a cost or expense in the current period. It reflects the portion of the value of fixed assets consumed during the period due to usage, passage of time, or technological obsolescence.

Current Period Indicator Value refers to the specific numerical value calculated according to a predetermined formula for a particular financial indicator (such as budget execution rate, return on equity, etc.) in financial analysis or performance evaluation, reflecting the actual operating or financial condition of the current accounting period (e.g., this month, this quarter, this year). It serves as the baseline data for comparative analysis against previous period values or budgeted values.

term_en.name: Discretionary Surplus Reserve Appropriated in Current Period

english: Current Period Appropriation of Discretionary Surplus Reserve
Discretionary Surplus Reserve Withdrawn in Current Period

definition_en: Discretionary surplus reserve appropriated in the current period refers to the portion of surplus reserve that a company appropriates from its current-period after-tax net profit at a certain ratio, based on the provisions of its articles of association or resolutions of the shareholders' meeting (or board of directors), and which is not legally mandated, during the current accounting period (e.g., the current fiscal year).

term_en.name: Statutory Surplus Reserve Appropriated in Current Period

chinese: 当期提取的法定盈余公积
english: Statutory Surplus Reserve Extracted in Current Period

definition_en: Statutory surplus reserve appropriated in the current period refers to the portion of retained earnings with specific purposes, which is calculated and appropriated from the after-tax net profit realized in the current accounting period (such as the current year or quarter) at the statutory rate of 10%, in accordance with the Company Law and other relevant regulations.

term_en.name: Production Expenses Incurred in Current Period

english: Production Expenses Incurred in the Period

definition_en: Production expenses incurred in the current period refer to the total of various actual expenditures made by an enterprise during the current accounting period for producing goods or providing services. It reflects the value of resources invested in production activities during the period and serves as an important basis for calculating product costs and evaluating current operational efficiency.

Current period revenue refers to the total revenue realized by an enterprise during the current financial reporting period (such as the current month, quarter, or year) through daily operating activities including sales of goods, provision of services, or transfer of asset use rights.

In financial accounting, 'Current Period Amount' typically refers to the cumulative amount of relevant financial data generated by an enterprise during the current reporting period (such as the current month, current quarter, or year-to-date). The specific meaning must be determined based on the type of financial statement and preparation requirements. For example, in the income statement, it may refer to the amount incurred during the current month or the cumulative amount from the beginning of the year to the end of the current month.

english: Closing Accounts Receivable for the Period

definition_en: Accounts Receivable at Period End refers to the total amount of credit sales for goods or services provided that has not yet been collected from customers as of the end of the current accounting period (e.g., month, quarter, or year). It represents the company's outstanding receivables at a specific point in time and is an important current asset on the balance sheet.

english: Material Purchase Cost for the Period

definition_en: Current period material procurement cost refers to the total cost actually paid or payable by an enterprise during the current accounting period (such as a quarter or a month) for purchasing raw materials required for production. It typically includes the purchase price of materials, related taxes and fees, transportation costs, loading and unloading expenses, and other costs directly attributable to material procurement.

term_en.name: Write-offs and Recoveries for the Period

english: Write-off and Reversal Amount for the Period

definition_en: Write-offs and recoveries for the period refer to the total or net amount of bad debt actually written off (i.e., confirmed as uncollectible and charged off) by an enterprise during the current accounting period, plus the amount recovered (i.e., reversed) due to the partial or full collection of previously written-off bad debts in the current period. It reflects the actual change in the allowance for doubtful accounts during the period and is a key component in calculating the ending balance of the allowance for doubtful accounts.

term_en.name: Dividend Per Share for the Current Period

definition_en: Dividend per share for the current period refers to the amount of cash dividend actually paid per common share by the company during the current reporting period (typically a fiscal year or quarter), reflecting the direct cash return shareholders receive from the company's profits for that period.

term_en.name: Total Current Liabilities for the Period

definition_en: Total current liabilities for the period refer to the aggregate sum of all debts that a company is obligated to repay within one year or within one normal operating cycle (whichever is longer) as of the end of the current accounting period (e.g., the current quarter or fiscal year). It reflects the company's short-term debt repayment pressure.

term_en.name: Current Assets Ending Balance for the Period

chinese: 本期流动资产期末余额

definition_en: Current Assets Ending Balance for the Period refers to the total book value of all assets held by an enterprise at the end of the current accounting period (e.g., month, quarter, or year) that are highly liquid and expected to be realized, sold, or consumed within one normal operating cycle (typically one year or an operating cycle longer than one year).

Current Period Consumption Expenditure refers to the total amount spent by individuals, households, or businesses on purchasing goods and services within a specified current time period (such as a month, quarter, or year). It reflects the level of consumption activity during that period.

term_en.name: Current Period Surplus Reserve Transfer or Utilization Amount

english: Current Period Surplus Reserve Transfer-Out or Utilization
Utilization of Surplus Reserve in Current Period

definition_en: Current period surplus reserve transfer or utilization amount refers to the amount transferred out or utilized from the surplus reserve account by an enterprise during the current accounting period. This typically includes specific uses such as applying surplus reserve to cover losses, converting to capital (share capital), or distributing dividends, resulting in a decrease in the surplus reserve balance.

term_en.name: Net Profit After Tax for the Period

definition_en: Net profit after tax for the period refers to the amount of profit ultimately attributable to the owners of the enterprise within a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a year), after deducting all costs, expenses, and income tax expenses.

term_en.name: Increase in Current Operating Liabilities for the Period

chinese: 本期经营流动负债增加额
经营性流动负债本期变动
经营相关短期负债增加
english: Increase in Operating Current Liabilities for the Period

definition_en: Increase in current operating liabilities for the period refers to the growth in the total amount of liabilities arising from daily business operations (such as purchasing goods, receiving services, etc.) that are due for repayment within one year or one operating cycle, compared to the end of the previous period. It reflects the increased demand for short-term funds generated by the company's operating activities.

term_en.name: Increase in Operating Current Assets for the Current Period

chinese: 本期经营流动资产增量
经营性流动资产变动额
english: Increase in Operating Current Assets for the Period

definition_en: Increase in Operating Current Assets for the Current Period refers to the net increase in current assets (such as cash, accounts receivable, inventory, etc.) used for daily business operations during the current accounting period compared to the end of the previous period. It reflects the additional short-term operating resources invested by the enterprise to support business expansion or operations in the current period.

term_en.name: Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities for the Period

chinese: 经营活动现金流量净额
english: Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities

definition_en: Net cash flow from operating activities for the period refers to the difference between the total cash inflows and total cash outflows generated by a company's core, day-to-day business operations (such as sales of goods, provision of services, payments to suppliers, and employee compensation) during a specific accounting period (e.g., a quarter or a year). It reflects the company's ability to generate cash from its principal business activities and is a key indicator for assessing financial health and earnings quality.

english: Operating Current Liabilities for the Period

definition_en: Current operating liabilities refer to the debts incurred by an enterprise during the current accounting period due to daily operating activities (such as procurement, production, sales, etc.) that are expected to be repaid within a normal operating cycle (typically one year). They reflect the enterprise's reliance on short-term operating funds.

english: Long-term Operating Liabilities of the Period

definition_en: Current period operating long-term liabilities refer to debts with a repayment term exceeding one year that arise from a company's daily operating activities during the current accounting period (such as the current year or quarter). They reflect the liabilities the company undertakes to support its long-term operations, which require repayment over multiple future accounting periods.

Current dividend refers to the portion of profits that a company decides to distribute to its shareholders during the current financial period (such as the current quarter or fiscal year), typically paid in cash, serving as a means for shareholders to obtain returns from the company's earnings.

term_en.name: Increase in Current Period Operating Revenue

english: Increase in Operating Revenue for the Current Period

definition_en: The increase in current period operating revenue refers to the amount by which the total operating revenue realized by an enterprise in the current accounting period (e.g., this quarter or this fiscal year) exceeds the total operating revenue from the previous comparable accounting period (e.g., the previous quarter or the previous fiscal year). It reflects the growth of the enterprise's principal business activities during a specific period.

term_en.name: Discretionary Surplus Reserve Appropriated in Current Period

english: Current Period Appropriation of Discretionary Surplus Reserve
Discretionary Surplus Reserve Provision for the Period

definition_en: Discretionary surplus reserve appropriated in the current period refers to the portion of funds that a company appropriates from its current-period after-tax net profit, based on resolutions of the board of directors or shareholders' meeting, for specific purposes such as future development or covering losses. Unlike statutory surplus reserves, its appropriation ratio and usage are determined by the company itself and are not legally mandated.

term_en.name: Statutory Surplus Reserve Appropriated in Current Period

english: Accrued Statutory Surplus Reserve for the Period

definition_en: Statutory surplus reserve appropriated in the current period refers to the amount that an enterprise, in accordance with the provisions of the Company Law, appropriates from the current period's after-tax net profit at the statutory rate of 10% and records into the surplus reserve account during the current accounting period (e.g., the current year). It constitutes a significant component of the ending balance of surplus reserve.

The current period accrual amount refers to the sum calculated and set aside within the current accounting period based on a specified calculation base and rate, to be recorded as a current period cost, expense, or provision. Examples include accruals for bad debt provisions, depreciation expenses, or interest payable.

term_en.name: Purchase Price Variance for Goods Acquired in Current Period

chinese: 本期购进商品进销差价
english: Purchased Goods Price Difference in Current Period

definition_en: Purchase price variance for goods acquired in the current period refers to the total difference between the selling price and the purchase price (cost price) of goods purchased or processed and received by an enterprise during the current accounting period (e.g., this month, this quarter). It is a key component in calculating the gross profit margin rate on goods and is used to adjust merchandise sales revenue to cost of goods sold under the retail inventory method.

term_en.name: Original Value of Operating Long-term Assets Acquired in Current Period

chinese: 本期购入经营长期资产原值
当期购置长期经营资产原值
经营用长期资产本期购置原值
english: Original Value of Operating Long-term Assets Acquired in Current Period
Cost of Long-lived Operating Assets Purchased This Period

definition_en: The original value of operating long-term assets acquired in the current period refers to the initial recognized cost at acquisition of tangible assets (such as plants, equipment, vehicles, etc.) purchased or constructed for business operations during the current accounting period (e.g., the current year or quarter), with an expected useful life exceeding one year, excluding subsequent depreciation or impairment.

term_en.name: Cost of Inventory Purchased in Current Period

english: Cost of Goods Purchased in Current Period
Current Period Purchase Cost of Inventory

definition_en: Cost of inventory purchased in the current period refers to the total cost actually paid or payable by an enterprise for purchasing inventory during the current accounting period (such as a month, quarter, or year). This typically includes the purchase price of inventory, related taxes and duties (e.g., customs duties), transportation costs, loading and unloading fees, insurance premiums, and other expenditures directly attributable to bringing the inventory to its intended salable condition.

term_en.name: Quantity of Inventory Purchased in Current Period

definition_en: Quantity of inventory purchased in the current period refers to the actual quantity of various types of inventory, such as raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished goods, newly acquired by an enterprise for production or sales during the current accounting period.

english: Cost of Goods Purchased in Current Period

definition_en: Current period purchase cost refers to the total cost incurred by an enterprise during the current accounting period to acquire inventory items such as goods or raw materials for production or sale, typically including purchase price, transportation fees, tariffs, packaging fees, and other directly related expenditures.

Quantity purchased in the current period refers to the physical quantity of inventory, such as raw materials or merchandise, actually purchased by an enterprise for production or sales during the current accounting period (e.g., a month, a quarter, or a year).

Current Period Amount refers to the total of relevant financial data occurring within a specific financial reporting period (such as monthly, quarterly, or annual). For example, in the income statement, it represents the cumulative occurrence of items such as revenue, expenses, and profit during the reporting period (this month, this quarter, or this year).

term_en.name: Total Current Period Long-term Operating Liabilities

definition_en: Total Current Period Long-term Operating Liabilities refers to the aggregate amount of liabilities arising from daily business operations (such as procurement, production, and sales) with repayment terms exceeding one year, as of the end of the current accounting period (e.g., the current fiscal year or quarter). It reflects the scale of debt that a company has undertaken to support its long-term operations and is due for repayment beyond one year in the future.

english: Working Capital Demand for the Period

definition_en: Current period demand typically refers to the total amount of working capital or liquid funds required by an enterprise to maintain normal production and operational activities during the current operating cycle or a specific period. It reflects the immediate funding needs generated by the enterprise to support daily operational activities such as sales, procurement, and production.

Scheduled purchases for the period refer to the quantity or value of raw materials, goods, or services planned to be procured within a specific upcoming timeframe (such as a quarter or a year) during the enterprise budgeting process, in order to meet production or sales demands. It serves as a critical link connecting the production budget, sales budget, and ending inventory budget.

term_en.name: Estimated Cost of Sales for the Current Period

definition_en: Estimated Cost of Sales for the Current Period refers to the pre-estimated cost corresponding to products to be sold or services to be provided within the current accounting period (such as monthly, quarterly, or annual), based on sales forecasts. It serves as a crucial basis for cost budgeting and profit forecasting in an enterprise.

Estimated usage for the period refers to the quantity or value of inventory items such as raw materials, supplies, and merchandise that a company expects to consume or use during a specified budget or planning period. It serves as a crucial intermediate figure in preparing production budgets, direct materials budgets, and inventory budgets, used to project ending inventory levels or procurement requirements.

term_en.name: Unit Cost of Inventory Prior to Current Shipment

english: Unit Cost of Inventory Prior to Shipment

definition_en: Unit cost of inventory prior to current shipment refers to the average cost per unit (e.g., per piece, per kilogram) of a specific batch of inventory calculated before the enterprise dispatches (sells or withdraws) that batch. This cost is typically determined based on the inventory valuation method chosen by the enterprise (such as FIFO, weighted average method, etc.) and is used to ascertain the cost of goods issued and to carry forward the cost of sales.

Current purchase quantity refers to the actual physical quantity of goods or raw materials purchased by an enterprise within a specific current accounting period (such as the current month or quarter) to replenish inventory or meet sales and production needs.

Marginal tax rate refers to the statutory tax rate corresponding to the specific income bracket into which a taxpayer's taxable income falls under a progressive tax system. It is the tax rate directly applied when calculating the tax payable, typically used in conjunction with a quick calculation deduction to simplify the tax computation process.

Principal Present Value refers to the value of the original capital invested at the beginning of an investment or financial calculation at the calculation point in time. When considering the time value of money, it typically refers to the discounted present value of the principal corresponding to a future series of cash flows, serving as the basis for calculating investment returns and future values.

Principal terminal value refers to the total value achieved by the initially invested principal at the end of a specific investment period, after appreciation over time (such as through interest, dividends, or capital gains). It reflects the final outcome of the principal after considering the time value of money and investment returns.

Weight refers to the numerical value assigned to each data item or indicator in the calculation of a weighted average or comprehensive evaluation to reflect its relative importance. A larger value indicates a greater influence of that data item in the overall calculation.

Market value of equity typically refers to the total value of all outstanding shares of a company calculated at the current market price. It reflects the market's overall assessment of the company's future profitability and growth potential, differing from the owner's equity (book value) on the balance sheet, which is measured based on historical cost.

chinese: 归属于股东的自由现金流

definition_en: Free Cash Flow to Equity refers to the residual cash flow available to the company's shareholders after meeting all operating expenses, taxes, debt interest and principal repayments, and necessary capital expenditures. It reflects the theoretical cash return available to shareholders and serves as a crucial foundation for evaluating a company's equity value.

Net material consumption refers to the quantity of materials directly required to constitute the final engineering entity or product entity in construction projects or production processes, excluding unavoidable losses and waste generated during transportation, processing, and operations at the construction or production site.

Material Standard Consumption Quantity refers to the total amount of materials required to complete a planned production output, calculated based on the material standard (standard consumption) per unit product and the planned production volume in the production budget or cost budget. It links production planning with material procurement/consumption budgets and serves as a critical component in cost control and budget preparation.

Actual material consumption quantity refers to the physical amount of raw materials, auxiliary materials, and other supplies actually consumed for producing goods or providing services during a specific production cycle or cost accounting period. It serves as fundamental data for cost calculation and variance analysis, used to compare with standard or planned consumption quantities to evaluate material usage efficiency.

Material cost refers to the value of raw materials, auxiliary materials, and other supplies consumed by an enterprise in the process of producing goods or providing services. It is a significant component of product cost, reflecting the primary consumption in the production phase, and serves as the foundation for cost control and product pricing.

Material wastage rate refers to the percentage of material loss caused by accidents, human operations, or natural factors during production or construction processes, relative to the planned net usage of that material. It is a key metric for measuring material usage efficiency and cost control, commonly used in establishing material consumption quotas.

Beginning inventory of materials refers to the actual quantity of raw materials, supplies, and other inventory items available for production or sale in a company's warehouse at the start of an accounting period (such as a month, quarter, or year). It serves as a critical baseline data point for preparing procurement budgets and production plans.

english: Standard Price per Unit of Material

definition_en: Material standard price refers to the predetermined unit price that an enterprise should pay for a specific material consumed in producing one unit of product under normal operating conditions, within the standard costing system. It serves as the basis for calculating direct material standard costs and conducting cost variance analysis.

Standard Material Usage Quantity refers to the predetermined quantity standard of raw materials that should be consumed to produce a unit of product or complete a specific task under standard costing, based on technical specifications, historical data, and efficiency expectations. It serves as one of the bases for calculating direct material cost variances.

Estimated ending inventory of materials refers to the quantity or value of raw materials, auxiliary materials, and other inventory items that a company expects to hold at the end of a budget or planning period (e.g., month-end, quarter-end, or year-end). It is a key input for preparing the direct materials purchase budget and the production budget, used to ensure production continuity and control inventory costs.

Estimated material requirement refers to the total quantity of raw materials needed to be consumed to complete the projected production tasks during a specific budget or planning period. It is calculated based on the material consumption quota per unit product and the estimated production volume, serving as fundamental data for preparing material procurement budgets and production cost budgets.

Material cost refers to the expenses incurred for various raw materials, auxiliary materials, purchased semi-finished goods, fuel, power, packaging materials, etc., that are directly consumed and constitute the physical entity of the product during the production of goods or provision of services. It is a significant component of product cost.

term_en.name: Taxable Income Derived from a Specific Country (Region)

english: Taxable Income from a Foreign Country (Region)

definition_en: Refers to the income derived by a Chinese resident enterprise or non-resident enterprise from a specific country or region outside China, which is subject to calculation and payment of enterprise income tax according to the provisions of the Chinese Enterprise Income Tax Law. This portion of income must be considered separately when calculating the enterprise's total global taxable income and may involve the credit for foreign taxes already paid.

term_en.name: Taxable Income Derived from a Country (Region)

chinese: 境外所得应纳税所得额
来源于境外的应税所得
english: Taxable Income from a Foreign Country (Region)

definition_en: Taxable income derived from a country (region) refers to the portion of income earned by a Chinese resident enterprise or individual from sources outside China, in a specific foreign country or region, which must be included in the taxable income when calculating enterprise income tax or individual income tax according to Chinese tax laws. This income may have been subject to income tax in the foreign jurisdiction and may be eligible for foreign tax credit upon repatriation to China in accordance with relevant regulations.

The limit is a core concept in calculus, describing a definite value that a function value (or term value) approaches infinitely as the independent variable (or term number) approaches a specific value. It serves as the foundation for understanding concepts such as derivatives and integrals.

Structure loss value refers to the direct property loss amount caused by the destruction, damage, smoke contamination, water damage, or demolition of independent buildings or structures such as houses, bridges, and chimneys due to unexpected events like fires or accidents. This value is typically calculated based on factors such as replacement value, degree of depreciation, and burn damage rate, and is a crucial component in assessing actual losses.

The allocation basis for a product refers to the quantitative foundation or measure, closely related to the incurrence of product costs, used as the basis for apportioning indirect costs (such as manufacturing overhead, administrative expenses, etc.) to different products. Common bases include product output, weight, volume, production value, raw material consumption, or standard cost.

term_en.name: Foreign Tax Credit Limitation for a Specific Country (Region)

english: Credit Limitation for Foreign Income Tax

definition_en: The foreign tax credit limitation for a specific country (region) refers to the maximum amount of income tax paid in that particular country (or region) that a Chinese enterprise is allowed to credit against its Chinese corporate income tax liability calculated on its worldwide income. Its purpose is to avoid international double taxation while preventing enterprises from improperly reducing their domestic tax obligations in China by utilizing foreign tax credits.

term_en.name: Market Value of a Class of Capital

definition_en: The market value of a class of capital, typically referring to equity capital (such as common stock), is the total price investors are willing to pay in the open market to acquire all of a company's equity. It reflects the market's comprehensive assessment of the company's future profitability and growth potential.

term_en.name: Book Value of a Class of Capital

definition_en: The book value of a class of capital refers to the amount of that capital measured and disclosed in the enterprise's financial accounting statements in accordance with accounting standards. It typically reflects the net amount of capital after deducting relevant provisions (such as depreciation, amortization, or impairment reserves) and represents the value recorded on the accounting books.

The Standard Activity Allocation Rate is a predetermined fixed allocation rate calculated based on budgeted or normal activity costs and activity volumes in Activity-Based Costing. It is used to allocate activity costs to cost objects (such as products or services), which can avoid the impact of fluctuations in actual activity costs on product costing and facilitates the provision of stable cost information for decision-making.

Standard Activity-Based Costing is a cost management method that integrates the concepts of standard costing and activity-based costing. It first establishes standard cost consumption rates for various activities (such as standard labor hours, standard material usage, etc.), then calculates the standard cost that should have been incurred based on actual activity volumes (such as actual production batches, actual service instances, etc.). This calculated standard cost is compared with the actual activity costs incurred to analyze cost variances, perform cost control, and evaluate performance.

Standard operating time refers to the time required for a worker with average proficiency, under suitable operating conditions and using the most appropriate operating method, to complete a specific task or operation at a normal working pace and with standard operating procedures. It serves as the basis for production planning, cost accounting, efficiency evaluation, and performance management.

Standard Activity Level refers to the predetermined level of operational activity or output quantity expected to be achieved under normal production conditions, used for establishing cost standards or allocating manufacturing overhead in standard costing or activity-based costing. It serves as a crucial benchmark for measuring efficiency, calculating cost variances, and implementing cost control.

Standard Other Labor Costs refer to the predetermined standard costs of various indirect or additional labor-related expenses, excluding basic direct labor wages, for completing specific production or service activities under the standard costing method. These costs typically include benefits, taxes, allowances, and subsidies, and constitute an important component of standard labor costs.

Standard base salary refers to the fixed foundational wage standard established by an enterprise according to its internal compensation system or industry practices for a specific position, job grade, or role, before considering factors such as performance, allowances, or overtime. It typically serves as the benchmark for calculating total labor costs, overtime pay, social insurance contribution bases, etc.

Standard base freight refers to the fundamental freight component in cargo transportation, calculated solely based on core billing parameters such as transportation distance, cargo weight, or volume, excluding surcharges, service fees, or other special charges. It constitutes the core component of the total freight cost.

Standard inventory cost refers to the predetermined unit cost standard established by an enterprise for internal accounting and control purposes regarding the production or holding of inventory (such as raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished goods) in financial and cost management. It is typically based on reasonable estimates of direct materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead, and is used to compare with actual incurred costs for variance analysis and performance evaluation.

Standard Cost Driver Rate refers to a predetermined allocation rate used in Activity-Based Costing to assign costs from activity centers to cost objects (such as products or services). It is typically based on budgeted or standard costs, calculated by dividing the estimated total cost of an activity center by the estimated total quantity of the cost driver, and is used for cost control and variance analysis.

Standard material cost refers to the predetermined direct material cost that should be incurred under normal production conditions for producing a unit of product under the standard costing method. It is typically calculated by multiplying the standard quantity of materials by the standard price of materials, and is used for cost control, budgeting, and performance evaluation.

Standard welfare expenses refer to the costs that an enterprise accrues or calculates in advance for various employee benefits (such as medical expenses, hardship allowances, canteen, childcare facilities, etc.) in accordance with national regulations or internal standards, typically calculated as a fixed percentage (e.g., 14%) of the total payroll.

Standard tax and fee refers to a pre-established or commonly applicable benchmark or reference value for calculating taxes and fees for a specific category of economic activities or cost items (such as standard labor cost) under particular regulations, policies, or industry practices. It is typically used in cost accounting, budget preparation, or financial analysis to provide a uniform and standardized basis for estimating taxes and fees.

Standard stockout cost refers to the expected or standardized loss cost incurred due to inventory supply interruption or insufficient stock that fails to meet customer demand under the standard costing method. It is typically estimated as a component of the total standard material procurement cost and is used for cost control and budget management.

Standard ordering cost refers to the estimated costs incurred to complete one standard purchase order under the enterprise's standard cost accounting system, serving as a fundamental component in establishing the total standard material procurement cost.

Standard error is an indicator that measures the dispersion between a sample statistic (such as the sample mean) and the population parameter. It reflects the magnitude of sampling error, i.e., the average error that may occur when using a sample to estimate the population.

Standard freight and miscellaneous charges refer to the predetermined standard cost or rate used in financial accounting or cost accounting for calculating and measuring transportation and related miscellaneous expenses associated with material procurement or goods transportation. It is typically based on historical data, industry standards, or contractual agreements, and is used for budgeting, cost control, and variance analysis. It is an essential component of the total standard procurement cost of materials.

term_en.name: Standard Freight and Miscellaneous Rate Coefficient

english: Standard Freight and Miscellaneous Rate Coefficient

definition_en: The Standard Freight and Miscellaneous Rate Coefficient is a pre-determined ratio or multiplier used to calculate the total standard freight and miscellaneous charges. It is typically determined by logistics companies based on comprehensive factors such as market conditions, transportation distance, and cargo type, and can be adjusted according to the specific requirements of the shipper. It serves as a key parameter in the freight and miscellaneous charge calculation model.

Standard Purchase Quantity refers to the optimal order quantity calculated using specific models (such as the Economic Order Quantity model) that minimizes total inventory costs (including purchase costs, ordering costs, and holding costs) while meeting production or sales requirements. It serves as a key reference standard for inventory management and procurement decision-making.

term_en.name: Historical Return of Underlying Asset Price

definition_en: Historical return of underlying asset price refers to the rate of return generated by price changes in a specific asset (such as stocks, bonds, commodities, etc.) over a past period, typically used to analyze the asset's historical profitability and risk characteristics.

Underlying asset price volatility is an indicator used to measure the uncertainty or degree of risk of future price movements of an underlying asset (such as stocks, commodities, etc.), typically expressed as a percentage. Higher volatility indicates that the asset price may experience larger upward or downward movements over a future period, implying greater uncertainty.

Underlying asset market price refers to the price agreed upon in a fair transaction between willing buyers and sellers in an open, active, and orderly market at a specific point in time. It reflects the consensus of market participants on the value of the asset and serves as a crucial reference for asset valuation, financial derivative pricing (e.g., options), and financial analysis.

term_en.name: Current Market Price of the Underlying Asset

english: Current Market Price of the Underlying Asset

definition_en: The current market price of the underlying asset refers to the prevailing, observable real-time transaction price of that asset in the open market at the time of valuation or transaction.
